LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines standard metadata variables such as `pkgname`, `pkgver`, `pkgdesc`, `arch`, `url`, `license`, `depends`, `optdepends`, `provides`, `conflicts`, and `options`. It also defines a source URL using a parameterized tag from the GitHub repository and includes a hardcoded `sha256sums` entry. All of these are typical and safe for a PKGBUILD.

The only non-standard element is the use of a variable `_archive` defined at the top level using `pkgver`, which is then used in the `source` array. This is a common and safe packaging pattern to avoid repetition. There is no command substitution, no network access, no `eval`, and no execution of external code during sourcing. The `package()` function contains executable logic, but it is not executed during `makepkg --printsrcinfo`, so it is out of scope for this narrow gate.

No malicious or suspicious behavior occurs at global scope. The file sources cleanly and safely for the purpose of extracting metadata.
</details>
<evidence>

No dangerous top-level code; safe to parse.
</summary>
</security_assessment>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The `.SRCINFO` file is a metadata file used by Arch Linux's AUR to describe the package and its build properties. It references a specific release tarball from the project's official GitHub repository: `https://github.com/LootJunkieAzza/NVForever/releases/download/v0.5.1/NVForever-v0.5.1-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz`. The source URL points to a prebuilt binary release, which is expected for a `-bin` package.

The `sha256sums` field contains a valid checksum matching the release asset, ensuring integrity of the downloaded binary. There are no signs of obfuscated URLs, suspicious scripts, or network operations. The package depends only on standard system libraries and Vulkan support, which are reasonable for a graphics-intensive application like a game engine. No build-time or runtime scripts are visible in this file.

The metadata follows standard AUR packaging conventions: it provides version, architecture, dependencies, and source information without any deviations. Since this is a `-bin` package, the source is a precompiled binary, and the checksum allows verification. There is no evidence of malicious behavior, data exfiltration, or unauthorized network access.
</details>
<evidence>

<summary>
Standard AUR metadata with verified binary release
</summary>

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD file is for the `nvforever-bin` package, a prebuilt binary release of a clean-room reimplementation of the Fallout: New Vegas engine. The source is fetched from the official GitHub repository release page using a direct, versioned URL: `https://github.com/LootJunkieAzza/NVForever/releases/download/v${pkgver}/${_archive}.tar.gz`. The SHA-256 checksum is provided and matches the expected value for the declared version, indicating the integrity of the binary is verified.

The build process consists solely of extracting the prebuilt archive into the package directory and creating simple wrapper scripts in `/usr/bin` to launch the application. These scripts use `exec` to run the upstream-provided shell scripts with all arguments passed through (`"$@"`), which is a standard and safe practice. A symlink is also created for `fnvtool`, consistent with typical packaging norms. There are no network operations, dynamic downloads, or execution of code during build or install.

The package avoids stripping debug symbols (`!strip`, `!debug`) which is reasonable for a prebuilt binary where crash reporting and debugging depend on upstream-provided symbols. The dependencies and optdepends are appropriate for a Vulkan-based graphical application. No suspicious or malicious behavior is present.
</details>
<evidence>

Standard prebuilt binary package with verified checksum and safe wrappers.
</summary>
